title: Pervomaisk
summary: Pervomaisk is a term commonly used in the former Soviet Union, originating from the May Day holiday, known as International Workers' Day. In the context of Ukraine, it refers to several locations within the country.

sections.heading: Etymology and Significance
paragraphs: The name Pervomaisk is derived from the holiday May Day, which is celebrated on May 1st and is recognized as International Workers' Day. This toponym reflects the historical and cultural significance of the holiday in the regions of the [[post-soviet-states|former Soviet Union]].

sections.heading: Pervomaisk in Ukraine
paragraphs: [[coal-in-ukraine|In Ukraine]], Pervomaisk refers to multiple locations, indicating that the name is not unique to a single place. The presence of these locations highlights the widespread use of the term within the [[ukrainian|Ukrainian]] context.

sections.heading: Pervomaysk in Russia
paragraphs: The term Pervomaysk is also used in Russia, where it designates multiple places. This illustrates the shared cultural heritage and historical connections between [[ukraine|Ukraine]] and Russia stemming from the Soviet era.

sections.heading: Related Terms
paragraphs: Several other terms are associated with Pervomaisk, including Pervomaisc, which refers to toponyms in Moldova, and Pervoye Maya, which relates to the May Day holiday. Additionally, Pervomaiske Raion is a district located in [[crimean-khanate|Crimea]], Ukraine, further emphasizing the relevance of the name within Ukrainian geography.
